Super Micro Stock Has Disappointed for a Year: Why Raymond James Sees 107% Upside ©@primeimages from Getty Images Signature via Canva, @Ali Raza via Canva
Key Takeaways

Raymond James raised its Super Micro Computer price target to $65 from $48 on Nov. 4, 107% above the Nov. 3 close, after a year in which the stock fell 40%.

Super Micro's September-quarter revenue rose 298% to $19.9 billion, and management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $72 billion to $82 billion.

The $65 target works out to about 14x forward earnings, close to the stock's five-year average. But the company still used $434 million of operating cash last quarter, and one customer took 44% of revenue.

A rebound looks reasonable, but until Super Micro's operating cash flow turns positive, the Street's $43 average target is the more likely place for the stock to land within a year.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) just reported a quarter in which revenue nearly quadrupled, and the stock is still down 40% over the past year. Raymond James sees a big rebound: on Nov. 4, analyst Simon Leopold kept his Outperform rating and raised his target to $65 from $48, 107% above the $31.39 close on Nov. 3.

A miss, an indictment and a $5.6 billion raise

The slide started on Nov. 4, 2025, when Super Micro reported September-quarter revenue of $5.0 billion, short of its own $6 billion to $7 billion guidance.

On March 19, US prosecutors charged co-founder Wally Liaw and two others with diverting about $2.5 billion of servers built with Nvidia chips to China. A board investigation cleared current senior management, but Liaw's trial isn't until March 2027.

Then came the bill. Free cash flow was negative $7.0 billion in the year to June 2026, and Super Micro raised $5.6 billion that month, selling common and mandatory convertible preferred stock.

A blowout quarter and a higher target

September-quarter revenue rose 298% to $19.9 billion, above even the preliminary range Super Micro gave in October, and adjusted EPS of $1.81 crushed guidance of $1.01 to $1.10. Management also raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $72 billion to $82 billion.

Raymond James named the main risk itself: customer concentration, and the chance that the biggest customer moves to white-box servers as it scales. One customer took 44% of the quarter's revenue.

Does $65 add up?

title: Super Micro Sinks 6%, Flex Down 13% as Election Raises Fears of “Data Center Moratoriums”

Super Micro Sinks 6%, Flex Down 13% as Election Raises Fears of “Data Center Moratoriums”
Michael Douglass

SMCI
Trade SMCI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Super Micro Sinks 6%, Flex Down 13% as Election Raises Fears of "Data Center Moratoriums" ©@Tiero via Canva
Key Takeaways

Super Micro fell 6% today, alongside Flex, on fears of Texas limits on data center construction after Tuesday's midterms.

Super Micro's full-year gross margin guide of 11.8%-12.2% sits below the quarter's 12.8%, and one customer made up 44% of revenue.

The stock traded at 6.4x forward earnings before today's drop, a discount likely to hold until its sales turn into cash.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) sank 6% today as Tuesday's midterms dragged down AI hardware stocks.

Flex (FLEX:NASDAQ) fell 13% with no news of its own. Its data center business is its fastest-growing: cloud and power infrastructure revenue rose 54% to $2.5 billion last quarter.

A moratorium in the biggest market

In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who promised a data center moratorium, unseated Gov. Greg Abbott.

Texas accounts for more than 25% of planned US data center capacity through 2030, according to Yahoo Finance. Raymond James analyst Ed Mills said a strong Democratic showing there could mean "increasing concerns about data center moratoriums and more restrictive AI regulation."

Data center builders and landlords fell even harder: Comfort Systems USA (FIX:NYSE) fell 16%, Quanta Services (PWR:NYSE) lost 12% and Texas Pacific Land (TPL:NYSE) dropped 14%.

The quarter had a catch of its own

The beat was huge: record revenue of $19.9 billion for the quarter ended Sept. 30, and a fiscal 2027 sales outlook raised to $72 billion-$82 billion.

But adjusted gross margin fell to 12.8% from 17.6% in the June quarter as AI solutions grew to 71% of sales. CFO Mark Long guided to 11.8%-12.2% for the year. And one customer made up 44% of revenue.

Nor is the cash there yet: operations used $434 million as inventory climbed to $15.1 billion.

Analysts went into the report expecting fiscal 2027 earnings per share to rise 31%, while sales now look set to nearly double:

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2029 (years to June) (TIKR)

Long's margin guide is still above the roughly 10.3% analysts were modeling, so I'd expect those estimates to rise.

Cheap for a reason

Super Micro traded at 6.4x forward earnings before today's drop, less than half its five-year average:

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

At today's price, it's about 6x, right around its five-year low.

The way I see it, Texas is the smaller of Super Micro's problems. A moratorium would hurt Texas Pacific Land, Comfort Systems and Quanta most; Super Micro's customers can build elsewhere. Until its record sales bring in cash, I don't expect that 6x multiple to move much.

title: Super Micro gets BofA upgrade to price target, but margins remain a concern
detail:
Super Micro gets BofA upgrade to price target, but margins remain a concern
Proactive
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 11:08 AM MST 2 min read
SMCI
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Super Micro gets BofA upgrade to price target, but margins remain a concern Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Super Micro Computer Inc (NASDAQ:SMCI) received a higher price target from Bank of America at $39 as stronger guidance failed to dispel concerns about margin sustainability.

Management raised its fiscal year 2027 revenue guidance to $72 billion to $82 billion and its gross margin outlook to 11.8%-12.2% following a strong fiscal first quarter.

Reflecting that outlook, the bank increased its fiscal year 2027 revenue and earnings per share forecasts to $81.2 billion and $6.34, respectively, from $79.6 billion and $5.31.

Super Micro Computer's target rose from $38, retaining a valuation of seven times estimated calendar year 2028 earnings per share, revised to $5.60 from $5.50.

Despite those increases, the broker questioned the durability of favorable non-AI server pricing and warned that a larger contribution from lower-margin AI deals would weigh on profitability.

Competition, component costs, and additional engineering support and services spending compound those pressures, with the bank expecting lower margins in the second half of fiscal year 2027.

Beyond profitability, substantial working capital needs underpin its forecast for continued negative free cash flow, while persistent material weaknesses in financial reporting controls add to its concerns.

Super Micro Computer also has high customer concentration in revenue and receivables, although management expressed confidence in its customers' credit quality, the bank said.

Balancing these risks, the broker highlighted strong AI demand and partnerships with Cisco, NetApp and Nutanix that support the company's efforts to reach more enterprise customers.

It also viewed capacity exceeding 8,000 racks monthly as a competitive advantage, with modular data center offerings potentially appealing to customers seeking faster deployment.

Funding remains a consideration, however, as management's lack of current capital-raising plans over the next 12 months depends on opportunities, with debt seemingly preferred over equity, the bank said.

Shares of Super Micro were down around 4.3% on Wednesday.

title: SMCI earnings analysis: questions answered and next catalysts

SMCI earnings analysis: questions answered and next catalysts
Investing.com
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 11:02 AM MST 3 min read
SMCI
Trade SMCI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Super Micro Computer (SMCI) reported FY2027 Q1 on Nov 3, 2026, and the numbers were large. The stock still trades at $30.28 (-3.55%) as of Nov 4, 12:25 PM EST. The after-hours pop of about +8–10% has faded. The stock is down -30.9% over one month (snapshot as of Nov 4, 2026).

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

EPS: $1.81 vs $1.23 est (+47% surprise).

Revenue: $19.90B vs $16.26B est, up 298% year over year.

Gross margin: 12.8% non-GAAP, above management's range.

AI mix: AI solutions were 71% of revenue, up from 59% the quarter before.

Questions Answered

Is demand real? Yes. Backlog hit a record even after revenue rose 79% sequentially.

Is margin erosion over? For now. Gross margin has fallen from 18.0% (FY2023) to 10.8% (FY2026). FY2027 guidance is 11.8%–12.2%, against a consensus of about 10%, per Rosenblatt (Nov 4, 2026).

Will guidance rise? FY2027 revenue guidance went to $72B–$82B from $65B–$72B. Q2 guidance is revenue of $19.5B–$21.5B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.66–$1.90. That is well above the consensus Q2 EPS of $1.14.

Are analysts convinced? Raymond James raised its target to $65 from $48. Rosenblatt kept $57 and Needham kept $46 (source, Nov 4, 2026).

Questions Still Open

Customer concentration: One large data-center customer was 44% of revenue. Losing or delaying that customer would hurt badly.

Back-half fade: Guidance implies second-half revenue about 10% lower than the first half, with margins about 100 bps lower.

Competition: Mizuho cut its target on competitive concerns, per the Nov 4 article above. Rising AI-server competition is the bear case for margins.

Funding and dilution: Management stressed matching funding to working capital. It also committed to being transparent about dilution and maturities. The preferred dividend is about $75M per quarter.

Estimate gap: The earnings feed shows Q2 consensus EPS of $1.14 on $18.11B revenue. The FinQL feed shows $1.25 on $15.02B. Both are below guidance, so estimates look stale and likely to rise.

Next Catalysts

Estimate revisions. Consensus EPS was already up 35% over 90 days. The new guidance points to more upward moves. FY2027 consensus is $4.75 EPS on $70.27B revenue, at the low end of the new guided range.

Q2 FY2027 report, tentatively Feb 2, 2027. Consensus is EPS $1.14 and revenue $18.11B. Management's quiet period starts Dec 11, 2026.

Margin delivery. Hitting the 12%–12.5% Q2 gross margin would test whether the FY2027 guide holds.

Customer and financing news. Watch for new customers outside the 44% account, and for any capital raise.

Analyst moves. The target range runs from $46 to $65. The stock trades at roughly 5.6x forward P/E (FinQL, as of Jun 30, 2027 period), which is cheap if the earnings hold up.

According to Raymond James, the customer accounting for 44% of SMCI's revenue is most likely SpaceX.

The firm raised its price target on the stock to $65 from $48 and maintained an 'Outperform' rating,

Bank of America maintained an 'Underperform' rating despite raising its price target, while Mizuho cut its target and kept a 'Neutral' rating.

SuperMicro (SMCI) shares dipped to near a three-month low in morning trade on Wednesday, with analysts flagging the company's dependence on a single customer.

Raymond James raised its price target on the stock to $65 from $48 and maintained an 'Outperform' rating, according to a research note cited by TheFly. The firm said Super Micro's latest results and higher full-year forecast were encouraging, but noted that gross margins faced pressure with one customer accounting for 44% of sales.

According to Raymond James, the customer was most likely SpaceX (SPCX), though Super Micro did not publicly identify it. Customer prepayments covered most of the company's working capital needs, helping ease concerns about cash flow, the firm added.

SMCI stock rose as much as 10% after hours on Tuesday, before paring gains in pre-market trade. At the time of writing, the shares were down 4%, hitting lows last seen in early August.

SMCI stock price performance year-to-date on November 4 as of 11:00 a.m. ET | Source: Koyfin
SpaceX Link Puts Super Micro's Customer Concentration In Focus

SpaceX merged with Elon Musk's AI company xAI in February. A few months later, in June, Super Micro CEO Charles Liang posted on X that the company was "proud to co-build another new Gigawatt AI datacenter for SpaceX and XAI within a year."

Source: @charlesliang/X

While Super Micro has not officially identified the customer, the post offers a potential clue to Raymond James' assessment.

The unnamed customer accounted for 44% of Super Micro's revenue in its first quarter (Q1) results, up from 28% for the full previous fiscal year, Chief Financial Officer Mark Long said on the company's earnings call Tuesday.

Long said concentration "at this level is a consequence of the scale at which AI infrastructure is now being built." He added that he expected it to "stay elevated while these buildouts run."

AI Demand Drives Revenue Higher, But Margins Contract

Super Micro reported revenue of $19.9 billion in Q1, beating analysts' estimates of $16.26 billion, according to Koyfin. Earnings came in at $1.81 a share, compared with forecasts of $1.23.

The company also raised its revenue forecast for the fiscal year ending June 2027 to $72 billion to $82 billion, from a previous range of $65 billion to $72 billion.
